chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all of them, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Five prayers are not to be left under any circumstance: when you circumambulate the House, when you intend to enter the state of Ihram, the prayer of the eclipse, and when you forget [a prayer], pray it when you remember, and the funeral prayer.'

key_terms.تُحْرِمَ: To enter the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What are the five prayers that should never be left according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates five specific prayers that carry the weight of obligation or high emphasis, ensuring they are never neglected regardless of one's state. This enumeration highlights the structural integration of ritual acts—such as the prayer during Tawaf and upon entering Ihram—with essential communal duties like the Funeral Prayer (Salat al-Janazah) and responsive acts like the make-up for forgotten prayers. Scholarly tradition interprets this as a comprehensive guide to maintaining spiritual continuity, linking personal devotion with collective responsibility.
